clue.text: Survived Western Offensive by Germany

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading from right to left, so the word is turned round

parts.note: offensive in the sense of wicked or nasty
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A wartime account: someone came through a German attack on the Western Front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western Offensive' reads as a military campaign, but Western only tells you to turn the next word round.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lived through something is to have survived it, so the past tense is a synonym.

clue.text: Ground beset with game overwhelming northern resort

indicators.note: beset means surrounded on all sides, so the ground goes inside the game
to overwhelm is to engulf, so the game also swallows the single letter

parts.note: ground in the sense of terrain

explanation.surface: A northern seaside town besieged by sporting fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions happen at once: the game wraps both the abbreviation and the ground. Llandudno is a seaside resort in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a Victorian seaside resort on the north coast of Wales.

clue.text: Event-review process stopped by independent Conservative minister

indicators.note: a thing stopped by something is plugged by it, so the two letters go inside

parts.note: VAR is football's video assistant referee, which reviews incidents

explanation.surface: A political row: an independent Tory minister halts a review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' looks political, but here it is a member of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a Church of England priest, and minister is a general word for a clergyman.

clue.text: Society miss sort of bachelor bowled over

indicators.note: something bowled over is knocked upside down, which in a down answer turns it end to end

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree

explanation.surface: A debutante is swept off her feet by a type of eligible man.
explanation.definitionFit: A deb is a debutante, a young woman of high society making her formal entrance.

clue.text: Assigned place in central part of Ronaldsay

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the letters drawn from the island's name
only the core letters from the middle of the following word are kept

parts.note: the three letters at the centre of the nine-letter name
to place something is to locate it

explanation.surface: Someone was given a spot in the middle of North Ronaldsay, an island in Orkney.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb goes inside the extracted letters, splitting them two and one. North Ronaldsay is one of Scotland's Orkney islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Allocated and assigned both mean given out as a share or designated for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Blue river south of Arizona

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece south of another sits below it, so after it

parts.note: the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A river with blue water lies below Arizona.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is a bright sky blue colour, so it is a shade of blue.

clue.text: Publicans requiring large house along with taps

indicators.note: to tap a barrel is to pierce it and get inside, so this piece goes in

parts.note: the House of Lords, one chamber of the UK Parliament

explanation.surface: Pub owners need a big building and beer taps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taps' looks like beer taps in the pub picture, but it signals the joining word breaking in between the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord is the person who runs a pub, so publicans and landlords are synonyms.

clue.text: OAPs chatter about misfortune

indicators.note: about suggests moving the letters around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Pensioners gossip about bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: OAPs are old-age pensioners in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a great disaster, an extreme form of misfortune.

clue.text: Tense single twin daughters have softened

explanation.surface: A single parent of twin girls has mellowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' reads as the verb of the sentence, but it is wordplay for possess, so the definition stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Toned down means moderated or made less harsh, so it is a synonym for softened.

clue.text: Met up for coffee

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means the letters run from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to have met someone is to have faced them

explanation.surface: Arranging to meet someone for a coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf is coffee with the caffeine removed, so it is a kind of coffee.

clue.text: Dramatist essentially sends back your changes

indicators.note: changes means the letters get rearranged into a new order
the essence of a word is its heart, so only its middle letter is wanted

parts.note: the middle letter of the five

explanation.surface: A playwright returns a script to someone with their edits rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sends back' looks like a reversal, but back is anagram fodder, joined by your and the centre of sends. Alan Ayckbourn is a prolific English playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Alan Ayckbourn is a celebrated English playwright, so he is an example of a dramatist.

clue.text: It strengthens 21ac by initially increasing capacity

indicators.note: initially points to just the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for capacity

explanation.surface: Something builds up a fashion by adding volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a medicine or drink taken to invigorate, so it is something that strengthens.

clue.text: Lost leaders land in strait

indicators.note: things that are lost are all over the place, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Commanders who have lost their way come ashore in a narrow sea passage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dardanelles is the narrow channel in Turkey joining the Aegean to the Sea of Marmara, a strait.

clue.text: Software advanced in repeat sales finally rises in value

parts.note: an app is a software application

indicators.note: one letter is put inside the following word

parts.note: to recite is to repeat aloud from memory

indicators.note: finally picks only the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Software from repeat sales ends up gaining value.
explanation.definitionFit: When an asset appreciates its value goes up, so the verb means rises in value.

clue.text: Very good FBI agent withdrawn

indicators.note: something withdrawn is drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Fed is American slang for a federal agent

explanation.surface: Praise for an excellent FBI agent who has been pulled from a case.
explanation.walkthrough: DEF is hip-hop slang for excellent, short for definitive or definite.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, def means excellent or cool, so it stands for very good.

clue.text: Royal Engineer mostly stops surprise attack around exit

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, sitting inside it like a cork
turned around means the attack word is read from the end

parts.note: a raid is a sudden assault

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a sapper is a soldier of the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A military engineer largely halts an ambush near the way out.
explanation.walkthrough: Sapper, minus its last letter, sits inside the turned-round attack. A sapper is the traditional name for a soldier in the British Army's Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Exit as a verb means leave or vanish from view, which is what disappear means.

clue.text: Boffin starts to study colonised tiniest bats

indicators.note: starts are first letters, so the opening letter of each of the next two words is taken

parts.note: first letters of the two words

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A researcher studies a colony of very small bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals being studied, but it is slang for mad. Boffin is British slang for a scientist or expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert, especially a researcher.

clue.text: Senior academic barely checking small map finds beach walk

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or restrain, so the stripped word holds the other pieces
bare means stripped, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: a reader is a senior university lecturer in the UK
a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: A professor in skimpy clothes consults a little map to find the promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: Reader is a British academic rank just below professor; stripped of its outer letters, it wraps the small map.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a long open level promenade, typically along a seafront.

clue.text: Chat mainly on port wine

indicators.note: mainly means most of it, so the final letter goes
in an across answer, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port
to jaw is to chat informally

explanation.surface: Mostly gossip over a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port wine' reads as one phrase, but port is the city and wine alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Italy included in new sea-coast link

indicators.note: something included in another goes inside it
new means made afresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Italy is part of a fresh coastal connection.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate two things is to connect them in the mind, so the verb is a synonym for link.

clue.text: Compound found in bovine leather that's not hard

indicators.note: not hard asks for the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard to be removed

parts.note: an ox is a bovine animal
hide is animal skin used for leather

explanation.surface: A chemical present in soft cowhide.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hard comes from pencil grading.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen with another element.

clue.text: Work backing up on job ends in even more pointless delays

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a post is a position of employment

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for work runs backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: only the final letter of each of the following words is taken

parts.note: the last letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Office grumble: jobs that keep getting more futile.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone is to put off until later, so the verb postpones means delays.

clue.text: Heading for trouble, addicted to fashion

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its front, so the first letter is wanted

parts.note: someone on drugs is addicted to them

explanation.surface: A fashion victim is on the road to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Ton is a dated British word for the fashionable world, as in 'bon ton'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ton, from French, means fashionable style or high society, the world of fashion.

clue.text: Slim gentlemen's first obsession

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: What men have always craved most: being slim.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a thing about something is to be fixated on it, so thing can mean an obsession.

clue.text: Fake ancient hut, dodgy on the face of it

indicators.note: in an across answer, the jumbled piece is put on top of, so after, the single letter
the face of a word is its front, so just the first letter is kept
dodgy means unsound, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A supposedly old hut looks suspicious at first glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the face of it' reads as an idiom meaning apparently, but it says take the front of the word it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fake as an adjective means not genuine, which is exactly what inauthentic means.

clue.text: Bowled over, head journalist put in accord

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so in a down answer the word runs backwards

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: An editor-in-chief was so impressed that he agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled over' looks like amazed, and 'put in' like insertion; only the head word turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuned means adjusted to the right pitch, so instruments that are tuned are in accord or harmony.

clue.text: Brief project beginning for Bronski Beat

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: to project something is to throw it

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is wanted

explanation.surface: A short project marks the start of the 1980s synth-pop band Bronski Beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bronski Beat' reads as the band's name, but Beat alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular pulse, so it means a beat, as of the heart.

clue.text: Fool one heartless little sod

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter is cut out

parts.note: a divot is a small piece of turf, and sod means turf

explanation.surface: Calling someone a fool and a little sod, a mild British insult.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod looks like an insult, but here it means turf; a divot is the chunk a golf club tears up.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot and a fool are both a stupid person, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Girl and father consuming 27 somewhere in the Himalayas

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: an informal name for one's dad
the answer to 27 down is a container, and an urn is one

explanation.surface: A girl and her dad eating something on a mountain trek.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 points to the answer POT, and the clue wants a synonym of that, not the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Annapurna is a massif in the Nepalese Himalayas, one of the world's highest peaks.

clue.text: Picked up excellent container

indicators.note: lifted up means, in a down answer, the letters read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone collected a fine vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' often means a homophone; here it lifts the word for excellent upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot is a rounded vessel for holding things, so it is a kind of container.

clue.text: Opening publicity about female's place on Tyneside

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the joined pieces go round the female

parts.note: a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A launch campaign concerning a woman's home in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining wordplay to definition. Tyneside is the area around the River Tyne in north-east England, including Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateshead is a town on the south bank of the River Tyne opposite Newcastle.

clue.text: Submit for consideration British pork pie wraps

indicators.note: to wrap is to enclose, so the lie goes round the letter

parts.note: pork pie is rhyming slang for lie, and a tale is a lie

explanation.surface: A British pork pie wrapped in pastry, offered up for approval.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang a pork pie (or porky) is a lie. In British usage, to table a motion means to put it forward for discussion, the opposite of the American sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English, to table a proposal is to put it forward for discussion at a meeting.
